content.title: Strong dealmaking boosts profits at US banking giants
content.summary:
Robust dealmaking activity and strong trading results helped boost US bank earnings Tuesday despite lingering worries about a softening job market and a potentially overvalued stock market.- Stock market 'frothiness' -
More bank earnings will be released in the coming days, but Tuesday's batch showed increases all around with Citigroup profits rising 16 percent to $3.8 billion, Goldman Sachs up 39 percent to $3.9 billion and Wells Fargo up 9 percent to $5.6 billion.

content.title: Big Banks’ Earnings Offer Encouraging Consumer Picture as Economic Fears Linger
content.summary: JPMorgan Chase, the country’s largest lender, now expects one of its core credit quality measures to look more favorable this year.  Citigroup says a measure of delinquencies has improved from a year earlier.  “You see strong consumer spend and stable deposits,” Wells Fargo Chief Executive Charles Scharf told analysts Tuesday, “and those things just kind of paint a picture of a consistently strong consumer.”
